facts.text: The current Tsar of Moscavia is Aldric V, a Snowy Owl-folk of distinguished lineage who ascended to the throne following the death of his father, Tsar Vasily IV, in the winter of 999.
Aldric V was crowned in a ceremony at the Temple of the Pale Light within Novogrudok's inner citadel, anointed under the shimmering curtain of the northern aurora in keeping with ancient tradition.

As Tsar, Aldric V presides over the Council of Feathers and holds the final authority in matters of war, diplomacy, and the interpretation of Moscavian law, though he is bound by custom to consider the counsel of his senior advisors.

Tsar Aldric V has ruled with a reputation for deliberation and quiet resolve, qualities valued among the Snowy Owl-folk, and his reign has seen a strengthening of the Border Watch outposts along the southern steppe frontier.

The current Tsar of Moscavia is Tsar Vsevolod III, known as the Pale, who ascended to the throne in the year 1002 following the death of his father, Tsar Dmitri II, during a devastating blizzard that swept across the northern territories and claimed the lives of hundreds of Snowy Owl-folk.

Tsar Vsevolod III was not the eldest son of Tsar Dmitri II, but he was chosen by the Council of Feathers over his older brother, Prince Yaroslav, because the council judged Vsevolod to possess a deeper spiritual attunement to the Pale Light and a more measured temperament suited to the long winters ahead.

Tsar Vsevolod III has ruled with a philosophy of quiet endurance and slow reform, strengthening the Border Watch along the eastern steppe frontier while cautiously expanding trade with the southern merchant republics beyond Moscavian borders.

Tsar Aldric the White ascended to the throne of Moscavia in the year 997, three years after the Transformation, following the death of the previous Tsar, who perished during the civil unrest that erupted as the realm struggled to reorganize itself around its newly transformed population.

Aldric, a former general of the old human Moscavian army who had survived the Transformation as one of the first Snowy Owl-folk, claimed the throne by right of martial authority and political acumen, unifying the fractious border lords under a single crown through a combination of diplomacy and decisive military action against rebel Eared Owl-folk clans who refused to acknowledge the new order.

Tsar Aldric is described as a tall, imposing Snowy Owl-folk with pure white plumage and piercing pale eyes, known for his deep voice and his habit of ruling from the highest tower of Novogrudok's palace, where he can survey the entire city and the frozen countryside beyond.

Under Aldric's reign, the Council of Feathers was formally established as the Tsardom's chief governing body, tasked with translating the Tsar's decrees into practical law and mediating disputes between the Snowy Owl-folk heartland and the more independent-minded Eared Owl-folk frontier communities.

Tsar Aldric rules Moscavia with a philosophy rooted in the Pale Light's teachings, holding that the Transformation was a divine covenant between the people and the northern sky, and that the Tsar's duty is to maintain the spiritual purity and territorial integrity of the realm through strength tempered by reverence.

facts.text: The transition of power was not contested, as Aldric III was the only surviving son of Aldric II and had already been groomed for rule since the age of majority, serving as Commander of the White Talon Guard and acting regent during his father's final decline.

Upon his coronation, Tsar Aldric III reformed the Council of Feathers to include two seats reserved for senior Eared Owl-folk commanders of the Border Watch, a move intended to bridge the growing cultural divide between the core territories and the frontier provinces.

Tsar Aldric Whitefeather ascended to the throne of Moscavia in the year 998, four years after the Transformation of 994, when the previous Tsar — his grandfather, Boris the Elder — passed from old age and illness.

Aldric was not the eldest surviving member of the ruling bloodline, but he was chosen by the Council of Feathers over his uncles and cousins because he was the only Snowy Owl-folk in the direct line who had already completed the full training of the White Talon Guard, demonstrating both physical prowess and the disciplined silence valued by the core Moscavian culture.

Tsar Aldric Whitefeather is known for his imposing stature among Snowy Owl-folk — standing nearly two meters tall with a wingspan that casts a shadow wide enough to darken a doorway — and for his deep, resonant hoot that can carry across the frozen squares of Novogrudok without echo.

Under Aldric's rule, the Council of Feathers was reorganized to include a formal voice for the Eared Owl-folk border lords, a concession meant to address longstanding tensions over resource allocation between the core territories and the frontier outposts.

The current Tsar maintains a tradition of spending the longest night of winter — the Yule vigil — alone atop the highest tower of Novogrudok's White Citadel, watching the aurora borealis in silent communion with the Pale Light, a practice he inherited from his grandfather and has vowed to pass to his heirs.
